purpose: Acamprosate is used to help people who have stopped drinking alcohol stay sober. It reduces the uncomfortable feelings and cravings that can happen after quitting alcohol. It works best when used along with counseling or a support program.
how_it_works: When someone drinks heavily for a long time, their brain chemistry gets out of balance. Acamprosate helps restore that balance by calming overactive signals in the brain that cause cravings and anxiety after quitting. Think of it as helping your brain settle back to a more normal state without alcohol.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are diarrhea, nausea, gas, and stomach upset. Some people may also feel anxious, have trouble sleeping, or notice itching or a mild skin rash. Most side effects are mild and often improve over time.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, because this medication is processed entirely through your kidneys and the dose may need to be adjusted or the medication avoided. Do not use acamprosate if you are allergic to it or have severe kidney disease. It does not treat alcohol withdrawal symptoms and should only be started after you have already stopped drinking. Always let your healthcare team know all the medications and supplements you are taking.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is two 333 mg tablets (totaling 666 mg) taken three times a day — morning, afternoon, and evening. It is important to take it every day even if you feel well. If you have kidney problems, your doctor may lower your dose. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
